title: Choose your genre, reader, and length

stage.name: Genre and reader
stage.description: You know what kind of story it is, and who it's for.

intro: Knowing what you're writing, and for whom.

questions.prompt: Match each choice to what it means.
pairs: The kind of story, like mystery or memoir
Who the book is written for
How long the book will be
questions.why: These three choices shape everything that follows.

questions.prompt: Why does knowing your reader matter?
options: It shapes the tone, words and details you choose
questions.why: A book for young children and one for historians tell stories very differently.

questions.prompt: Novels and children's picture books are usually about the same length.
questions.why: Picture books often have fewer than a thousand words. Many novels have tens of thousands.

questions.prompt: What helps two people agree on what kind of relationship they're building?
options: Saying clearly what you're looking for, like marriage or a long-term partnership
Changing your answer to match theirs
Avoiding the topic to keep things light
questions.why: Clear, kind honesty early saves heartache later.

talk: What kind of relationship is each of you hoping for, in your own words?
